questions.topic_text: Topic 1.2: Branch account at invoice price with stock reserve for unrealised loading in closing stock
questions.question_html: Care, a retail business, opened a branch Omega on 1st January, 2025; all branch sales on credit. Goods supplied from Head Office, invoiced at 10% above cost. Transactions (Jan/Feb/March 2025): Goods sent to Branch (purchase price) 60,000 / 75,000 / 90,000; Sales as per branch monthly report 57,000 / 63,000 / 82,500; Cash received from debtors and remitted to HO 30,000 / 76,500 / 52,500; Returns to HO (invoice price) 1,800 / 900 / 3,600. Branch closing stock at 31st March, 2025: ₹80,100 at invoice-to-branch price. Record in HO books, showing balances as on 31st March, 2025 and the branch gross profit for the three months.
questions.answer_html:
Branch Account (books of Care, Head Office): To Goods sent to Branch A/c (2,25,000 total invoice value: 60,000+75,000+90,000, at 10% above cost) 2,47,500; To Goods sent to Branch A/c — returns loading (6,300 × 10/110) 573; To Stock Reserve (80,100 × 10/110) 7,283; To Net Profit (balancing figure, transferred to General P&L) 56,045. By Goods sent to Branch — Loading 22,500; By Goods sent to Branch — Returns 6,300; By Bank (cash remitted, 30,000+76,500+52,500) 1,59,000; By Balance c/d — Closing Branch Assets: Stock 80,100, Debtors (Sales 2,02,500 − Collections 1,59,000 = 43,500) 1,23,600. Total both sides ₹3,11,400.

Memorandum Branch Debtors Account confirms Debtors closing balance ₹43,500 (Sales 2,02,500 − Cash received 1,59,000).

Branch gross profit for the three months: ₹56,045 (the loading on goods sent, net of returns and closing stock reserve, represents the branch's realised gross margin for the period).
questions.mistake_text: Author’s Note: Some examinees forgot to create a stock reserve for the unrealised loading in the closing stock (still at invoice price, not yet sold), overstating the branch's reported profit.

questions.topic_text: Topic 1.5: Integral foreign operation - monetary items at closing rate, non-monetary at historical, income/expense at average rate

Credit — Incomes 1,32,000; Creditors 15,570; HO Control A/c 5,820. Average exchange rate during the year: 1 USD = ₹56. Fixed assets purchased at 1 USD = ₹55. Closing rate: 1 USD = ₹58. questions.topic_text: Topic 5.2: Branch stock at invoice price with a manager's commission reduced for the cost of an ascertained stock deficiency
questions.why: Rank 6 topic (Accounting for Dependent Branches); MTP May 2025 Set 2.
questions.question_html:
Alpha Ltd. has a retail shop under the supervision of a manager. The ratio of gross profit at selling price is constant at 25 per cent throughout the year to 31st March, 2025.

Branch manager is entitled to a commission of 10 per cent of the profit earned by his branch, calculated before charging his commission but subject to a deduction from such commission equal in 25 per cent of any ascertained deficiency of branch stock. All goods were supplied to the branch from head office.

The following details for the year ended 31st March, 2025 are given as follows:

questions.topic_text: Topic 7: Adj & Recon of Branch & HO Accounts

topics.topic_name: Adjustment and Reconciliation of Branch& Head Office Accounts

questions.why: Rank 21 topic (Adjustment and Reconciliation of Branch& Head Office Accounts); PYQ May 2026.
questions.question_html:
(i) Why goods are marked on invoice price by the head office while sending goods to the branch?

(ii) Rama Ltd. has a branch at Delhi, that closes its books of accounts every year on 31st March. This is an independent branch, which maintains comprehensive books of accounts for recording their transactions. You are required to show Journal Entries in the books of branch on 31st March, 2026 to rectify or adjust the following: (A) Head Office allocates ₹2,70,000 to the Branch as Head Office Expenses, not yet recorded by Branch. (B) Depreciation of Branch Fixed Assets, accounts kept by Head Office, not yet recorded in Branch Books ₹2,30,000. (C) Branch paid ₹2,80,000 as salary to a Head Office manager, debited by the branch to its Salaries A/c. (D) Head Office collected ₹2,60,000 directly from a Branch Customer on behalf of the Branch; intimation received by the branch only now, not recorded till now. (E) A remittance of ₹3,00,000 sent by the Branch has not yet been received by Head Office. (F) The Branch incurred Advertisement Expenses of ₹60,000 on behalf of another Branch. (G) Goods worth ₹1,50,000 dispatched by the head office, but the branch has received goods worth ₹1,10,000 till date of reconciliation; rest received subsequently. (H) Goods worth ₹25,000 returned by the branch to head office yet not received by the head office. (6 Marks)
questions.answer_html:
(i) Goods are marked on invoice price to achieve the following objectives: (a) to keep secret from the branch manager the cost price of the goods and profit made, so that the branch manager may not start a rival and competitive business with the concern; (b) to have effective control on stock, i.e. stock at any time must equal opening stock plus goods received from head office minus sales made at branch; (c) to dictate pricing policy to its branches; (d) to save work at branch because prices have already been decided.

(ii) Books of Branch – Journal Entries:

ENo entry in Branch Books is required (this affects only Head Office's own reconciliation, as cash-in-transit from the branch's remittance).

(v) A remittance of ₹15,000 sent by the Branch has not yet been received by the Head Office. (vi) Branch A incurred advertisement expenses of ₹3,000 on behalf of Branch B.

Books of Branch A — Journal Entries:

topics.topic_name: Methods of Charging Goods to Branches

questions.why: Rank 72 topic (Methods of Charging Goods to Branches); MTP January 2025 Set 2.
questions.question_html: Why goods are marked on invoice price by the head office while sending goods to the branch?
questions.answer_html: Goods are marked on invoice price to achieve the following objectives: (i) To keep secret from the branch manager, the cost price of the goods and profit made, so that the branch manager may not start a rival and competitive business with the concern; and (ii) To have effective control on stock i.e. stock at any time must be equal to opening stock plus goods received from head office minus sales made at branch. (iii) To dictate pricing policy to its branches, as well as save work at branch because prices have already been decided.
questions.mistake_text: Author’s Note: A common error is listing only the stock-control rationale for invoice pricing and omitting the equally important reason of concealing the cost/profit margin from the branch manager to prevent a rival business being set up.
